then.text: The band's back on stage, and your saw's still in the corner, being sentimental. We'll play your tune for as long as you like.
A heckler in the crowd and you put him in his place. That's the best bit of stage management I've ever seen.
Take this: a conch horn. Blown for centuries to call boats home. It'll keep the storm off you, or at least make the storm feel out-honked.

else.text: Instruments, all there! Only a heckler left: Heckler Sands, by the Ripsaw Bar. He says the saw's out of tune. Prove him wrong, politely.
Saw, drum, now the gourd shaker from the museum volunteer. Then the band can play.
The goatskin drum belongs to the Old Fisher. He keeps it in his boat. He's very protective.
The saw. The salt raker at the Salt Works keeps one. He doesn't use it for anything, he just likes it.
Disaster! Our ripsaw band's lost all its instruments to a hurricane party. We need a carpenter's saw, a goatskin drum and a gourd shaker.
Ripsaw's our national music. The saw is scraped with a screwdriver. It's louder than it sounds. Which is saying something.

then.text: Look after that drum. It's been through two hurricanes and a wedding.
Band's short a drum? Here, take mine. Goatskin, made by my grandfather. It's seen more parties than a bishop.

else.text: Drum? Not till the band has a saw. I'm not giving it up for nothing.
Johnny cake with fish, that's breakfast here. Johnny cake is a sweet fried bread. The name might come from 'journey cake' but nobody agrees on that either.

tci_salter.text: Look at that heap. Fresh sea salt, raked by hand. Grand Turk and Salt Cay shipped it all over the Atlantic.
The ponds are pink because of tiny algae and brine shrimp. Flamingos eat the shrimp and turn pink themselves. It's all very efficient, if you're a flamingo.

tci_birder.text: That's a Caribbean flamingo. Brine shrimp and algae turn them pink: no shrimp, no pink.
They stand on one leg to save body heat. They nest on mud mounds in shallow water, and they're thoroughly shy. Shh.

tci_donkey.text: A donkey regards you with the patience of a creature that has been on this island longer than the roads.

tci_pilot.text: I jog along the airstrip. It's the only flat bit of Grand Turk. A plane landed last week. I had to stop for it. Annoying.
There's a replica of John Glenn's space capsule down there. Locals say he'd have preferred somewhere less warm for splashdown.

tci_home.text: The flight home to Brize Norton? It goes when the runway's clear of donkeys.
Head home to RAF Brize Norton?

then.text: Lovely. Please keep hold of your hat and your donkey.

else.text: Take your time. We'll be here.

turks_caicos_bureau.text: Welcome to the bureau de change. Local money in, sterling out, or the other way round. A small fee, and a very small queue.

turks_caicos_homebound.text: Heading back to the mainland? Passage to RAF Brize Norton can be arranged whenever you like. Bring your own sandwiches.
